genxml.title: RAD4 graphics head registers
genxml.doc: Registers of the PsiTech RAD4 PCI graphics board (PCI 12d1:0104) as the vendor's IRIX 6.5 driver and X server use them: a PLX PCI 9060-compatible bus interface, board-local framebuffer, timing and control registers, and the RAMDAC's indexed registers. Grades here are the three the definition format allows. established covers what a public datasheet or the shipped binaries state outright, including what the driver does, and each doc says which. inferred covers inferences and approximations, with the limit stated in the doc.

struct.name: ROM_REMAP
struct.from: PLX PCI 9060 Data Sheet, version 1.2
struct.doc: Expansion ROM remap register. Software use: the driver writes it once at attach, with the top byte 0xe1. Nothing reads it back.

struct.name: BUS_REGION_DESCRIPTOR
struct.from: PLX PCI 9060 Data Sheet, version 1.2
struct.doc: Local bus region descriptor. Software use: the driver writes 0xf84303c3 at attach, which selects a 32-bit local bus.

struct.name: MAILBOX
struct.from: PLX PCI 9060 Data Sheet, version 1.2
struct.doc: Mailbox 0. Software use: the driver reads it at attach and skips its own mode and RAMDAC setup when it is nonzero, because it takes that to mean a firmware initialiser has run, and writes zero to it at the end of every attach. What a real card holds here after power-on is unknown.

struct.name: INTCSR
struct.from: PLX PCI 9060 Data Sheet, version 1.2
struct.doc: Interrupt control and status, with the bits the driver uses. The driver ORs 0x50900 into it at attach whether or not pixel DMA is enabled.

struct.name: EEPROM_CTL
struct.from: PLX PCI 9060 Data Sheet, version 1.2
struct.doc: Serial EEPROM control. Bits 24 to 27 drive the configuration EEPROM. Bits 3 to 0 are the PCI read command the DMA engines use (public datasheet): the driver replaces them at attach with its DMA read command setting, 0xc by default, and the only values it accepts are 0x6, 0xc and 0xe; request 126 changes them later.

struct.name: FLASH
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver (flash sector requests)
struct.doc: Parallel flash, 64 KiB in 128-byte sectors. Software use: the driver switches the bus region descriptor to 0xf84003c0, uses byte accesses at the address with its two low bits inverted, programs a sector with the usual three-byte unlock sequence (0xaa, 0x55, 0xa0; addresses in the kernel driver page), writes 128 bytes and polls the last one. The part is not identified; an AT29C512-compatible page-write flash fits the geometry (inferred).

struct.name: RGB561_INDEX_LO
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; IBM RGB561 Architecture, preliminary revision 1.1, pp. 1, 27
struct.doc: RAMDAC index, low byte, in the low eight bits of a 32-bit store. The identification with the RGB561 index-low port is inferred from the driver's use of it.

struct.name: RGB561_INDEX_HI
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; IBM RGB561 Architecture, preliminary revision 1.1, pp. 1, 27
struct.doc: RAMDAC index, high byte.

struct.name: RGB561_DATA
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; IBM RGB561 Architecture, preliminary revision 1.1, pp. 1, 27
struct.doc: RAMDAC single-cycle data port. The index advances after each access.

struct.name: RGB561_DATA_MULTI
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; IBM RGB561 Architecture, preliminary revision 1.1, pp. 1, 4
struct.doc: RAMDAC multi-cycle data port for tables whose entries are wider than a byte: two cycles per window attribute or gamma entry, three per colour or cursor table entry. The index advances once per complete entry.

struct.name: TIMING_H0
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver
struct.doc: Horizontal timing bank 0. Software use: the mode loader writes one word per four-pixel group of the horizontal total (at most 781 words in the driver's modes). The words are computed from the mode record by the loader, read in full, and bank 1 and the vertical bank are written the same way; the field names below are the loader's structure read against VESA-style timings (modes.md, timing words), not a hardware statement. The bank depth is not known: 1024 words is the room before the next bank.

struct.name: TIMING_H1
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver
struct.doc: Horizontal timing bank 1. Same use and limits as bank 0, but the loader sets only the line-end, sync-window and sync-level bits, never the two enable bits.

struct.name: TIMING_H3
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver
struct.doc: Horizontal timing bank 3. Same use and limits as bank 1, with the sync-window bit inverted relative to banks 0 and 1 and the sync-level bit equal to theirs for separate sync (sync type 0) and inverted for composite sync and sync on green. The loader also holds a pointer to the slot between banks 1 and 3 and never writes it.

struct.name: TIMING_V
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver
struct.doc: Vertical timing bank. Software use: one word per line of the vertical total, at most 1656 for the driver's modes, computed by the loader from the record. The depth is not known; 1656 is the largest count any shipped mode needs. The field names are the loader's structure read against VESA-style timings (modes.md, timing words).

struct.name: PLANE_MASK
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver and standalone X server
struct.doc: Pixel write mask. Software use: the driver programs 0xffffffff at attach and around its DMA descriptor stores; the X server programs 0x0fffffff at screen start, then 0x00ffffff for colour drawing and 0x0f000000 for the overlay nibble before stores, and paints the window-type nibble under 0xf0000000 through the rectangle-fill request. The driver's buffered path sets the mask to the request mask before a DMA upload and restores the previous one after the transfer has finished, which is how the mask is kept live for DMA data (inferred). That a store merges as old under the inverse mask or value under the mask is the generic plane-mask convention. Which mask bit reaches which board plane is unknown: the software only treats bits 23 to 0 as colour, 27 to 24 as overlay and 31 to 28 as window type.

struct.name: KM_MR
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; Philips SCC68681 product data, 6 April 2004
struct.doc: Channel A mode register: the first write after a command-register mode-pointer reset goes to mode register 1, the next to mode register 2. The driver writes 0x07 twice at initialisation, and 0x47 then 0x07 after finding a mouse. Low eight bits of the store.

struct.name: KM_SR_CSR_A
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; Philips SCC68681 product data, 6 April 2004
struct.doc: Channel A: reads give the status register (bit 0 receiver ready, bit 2 transmitter ready, the two the driver tests); writes set the clock select, which the driver sets to 0xff.

struct.name: KM_CR_A
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; Philips SCC68681 product data, 6 April 2004
struct.doc: Channel A command register, written only. Values used: 0x1a, 0x20, 0x30, 0x40, 0x50 (resets, with 0x1a disabling receiver and transmitter), 0x05 (enable both), 0x01 and 0x20 around a transmit.

struct.name: KM_DATA_A
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; Philips SCC68681 product data, 6 April 2004
struct.doc: Channel A receive and transmit data, low eight bits.

struct.name: KM_ACR
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; Philips SCC68681 product data, 6 April 2004
struct.doc: Auxiliary control register, written zero at initialisation.

struct.name: KM_ISR_IMR
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; Philips SCC68681 product data, 6 April 2004
struct.doc: Reads give interrupt status, writes set the interrupt mask. The driver uses bit 1 (channel A receiver ready) and bit 5 (channel B receiver ready), and ANDs the saved mask with the status in its handler. The saved mask is also what drives board control bit 7.

struct.name: KM_MR_B
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; Philips SCC68681 product data, 6 April 2004
struct.doc: Channel B mode register, used as register km_mr is for channel A.

struct.name: KM_SR_CSR_B
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; Philips SCC68681 product data, 6 April 2004
struct.doc: Channel B status on read and clock select on write, as for channel A.

struct.name: KM_CR_B
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; Philips SCC68681 product data, 6 April 2004
struct.doc: Channel B command register, written only.

struct.name: KM_DATA_B
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; Philips SCC68681 product data, 6 April 2004
struct.doc: Channel B receive and transmit data, low eight bits.

struct.name: KM_OPCR
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; Philips SCC68681 product data, 6 April 2004
struct.doc: Output port configuration, written zero at initialisation, which makes the output port bits plain outputs.

struct.name: KM_OPR_SET
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; Philips SCC68681 product data, 6 April 2004
struct.doc: Set output port bits. The driver uses bits 2 and 6 around a channel A transmit and bits 3 and 7 around a channel B transmit. Their wiring (inferred: open-collector drives of the PS/2 clock and data lines) is not documented.

struct.name: KM_OPR_RESET
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver; Philips SCC68681 product data, 6 April 2004
struct.doc: Reset output port bits, same bits as km_opr_set. Written 0xff at initialisation.

struct.name: BOARD_CONTROL
struct.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver
struct.doc: Board control and status. Software use: the driver clears bit 5 while it programs a mode and sets it afterwards, sets bit 1 to ask for an interrupt at the next frame and clears it around DMA transfers, and its interrupt handler tests bit 5. That bit 5 reports a frame event only while bit 1 is set is inferred. Bit 7 is set whenever the keyboard and mouse controller has any interrupt enabled and cleared when none is. The status in bit 5 is read only by the interrupt handler, through a stored pointer, and bit 1 is cleared there when it is set. The physical effects are unknown.

struct.name: RGB561_SYNC_CTL
struct.from: IBM RGB561 Architecture, preliminary revision 1.1, p. 27
struct.doc: Sync control. The mode routine writes 1, or 0x23 when the EEPROM selector field equals 2.

struct.name: RGB561_PLL_VCO
struct.from: IBM RGB561 Architecture, preliminary revision 1.1, pp. 27, 36
struct.doc: PLL VCO divider. M is bits 5 to 0 plus 65. Bits 7 to 6 hold the range code; that position is inferred, since it reproduces the clock field of all 13 driver modes to the hertz.

struct.name: RGB561_PLL_REF
struct.from: IBM RGB561 Architecture, preliminary revision 1.1, pp. 27, 36
struct.doc: PLL reference divider N, bits 4 to 0.

struct.name: RGB561_CURSOR_CTL
struct.from: IBM RGB561 Architecture, preliminary revision 1.1, pp. 3, 37
struct.doc: Cursor control. Bit 0 enables the 64 by 64 two-bit cursor.

struct.name: RGB561_CURSOR_HOT_X
struct.from: IBM RGB561 Architecture, preliminary revision 1.1, pp. 3, 38
struct.doc: Cursor hot spot, horizontal, six bits.

struct.name: RGB561_CURSOR_HOT_Y
struct.from: IBM RGB561 Architecture, preliminary revision 1.1, pp. 3, 38
struct.doc: Cursor hot spot, vertical, six bits.

struct.name: DMAMODE0
struct.from: PLX PCI 9060 Data Sheet, version 1.2
struct.doc: DMA channel 0 mode. Software use: the driver reaches the DMA registers through the expansion ROM resource, writes 0x7c3 here (32-bit local bus, chaining, done interrupt enabled) and clears the done-interrupt bit when a transfer times out.

struct.name: DMADPR0
struct.from: PLX PCI 9060 Data Sheet, version 1.2
struct.doc: DMA channel 0 descriptor pointer. Loaded from each descriptor's next-pointer word. The driver starts it at the top of the board's 8 MiB local memory.

struct.name: DMACSR0
struct.from: PLX PCI 9060 Data Sheet, version 1.2
struct.doc: DMA command and status, channel 0 in bits 7 to 0. The driver starts a transfer by writing 3 (enable and start) and aborts one with 4 after a timeout, then polls Done.

struct.name: DMA_DESC_NEXT
struct.from: PLX PCI 9060 Data Sheet, version 1.2, Table 51
struct.doc: Fourth word of a 16-byte chain descriptor (PCI address, local address, byte count, next pointer). It is loaded into the descriptor pointer register, and its low bits describe the descriptor's own transfer.

constant.name: DMA_DESC_BYTES
constant.from: PLX PCI 9060 Data Sheet, version 1.2, section 3.6.2

constant.name: FB_SIZE
constant.from: PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver (the mapping it requests)

constant.name: REFERENCE_CLOCK_HZ
constant.from: IBM RGB561 Architecture, preliminary revision 1.1, p. 36; PsiTech RAD4 release 1.3k driver
